Ticket Id: 25298

Dr Andrew McDonald
General surgeon
North Melburne Private Hospital
86 Elm Road
North Melboune 3051

23/1/ 2007

Dear Dr McDonald,
RE: Mrs Daniela Starkovic

Thank you for seeing Mrs Starkovic, a 45-year-old married woman whose features are suggestive of
cholelithiasis.

Mrs Starkovic firstly presented on the 20th of January 2007 with a 10 day history of epigastric pain. Her      Comment [teacher1]: days
pain was radiating to the right side, associated with nausea and constant for an hour. At night before she     Comment [teacher2]: The
visited me, the pain exacerbated as it was constant for 2 hours, colicky in nature, associated with vomiting
and not relieved by Aspirin. On examination, mild tenderness in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen        Comment [teacher3]: a
was detected. Otherwise, no abnormalities were observed.

Today, the patient was anxious and thinking of acquiring abdominal cancer in spite of cessation of pain.
Laboratory results revealed mild elevation of alkaline phosphatase level. Ultrasound showed multiple
gallstones in a small contracted gall bladder.

In view of the above, my provisional diagnosis is gall bladder inflammation and I reassured the patient
regarding the possibility of cancer. I would really appreciate it if you provide an assessment of Mrs
Starkovic and further management of her condition including the possibility of surgical management.

For any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely

Doctor
